questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, what happens to the ITSM Enhanced Security Features plugin (com.snc.itsm.enhanced_security) when an existing instance is upgraded?

options.text: It is activated automatically during the upgrade, adding "deny unless authenticated" ACL rules to several ITSM tables
It remains inactive and must be requested from ServiceNow Support
It is activated only on newly provisioned instances, as before
It is removed and its ACL rules are merged into the itil role

explanation.correct: The ITSM Enhanced Security Features plugin is now activated automatically on upgrade to Brazil (previously it was activated only on new instances). Activating it adds "deny unless authenticated" ACL rules to several IT Service Management tables. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-changemanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say the plugin is activated automatically on upgrade; Support is only involved if you want to revert to the pre-upgrade behavior.
This describes the previous behavior. The release notes say it is now activated automatically on upgrade as well.
The release notes say the plugin is activated and adds ACL rules; they do not describe removing it or merging rules into the itil role.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Change Management

documentation.section: Change Management - Important information for upgrading

source.excerpt: The ITSM Enhanced Security Features plugin is now activated automatically when you upgrade to the Brazil release.

questions.question: In the Australia release, the granular sn_change_admin role can be assigned to let users configure Change Management features and properties. Which roles does sn_change_admin include? (Choose three.)

itil_admin
sn_change_read_only

source.excerpt: The sn_change_admin role includes the sn_change_writer, change_manager, and sn_change_cab.cab_manager roles.

questions.question: In the Brazil release, a change request is scheduled inside an active change lockdown period. What does change lockdown conflict detection do with this change request?

options.text: Marks it with an Inside Change Lockdown conflict and places it on hold until it is rescheduled outside the lockdown period
Cancels the change request automatically
Converts it to an emergency change so it can bypass the lockdown
Sends it to the CAB for an override approval while it keeps progressing

explanation.correct: Change lockdown conflict detection flags change requests that overlap an active lockdown period. Such a change is marked as an Inside Change Lockdown conflict and placed on hold; rescheduling it outside the lockdown clears the conflict so it can continue processing. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-changemanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say the change is placed on hold, not cancelled.
The release notes describe placing the change on hold and rescheduling it; they do not describe converting it to an emergency change.
The release notes say the change is placed on hold and must be rescheduled outside the lockdown; no CAB override path is described.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Change Management

source.excerpt: Any change request inside a lockdown is marked as an Inside Change Lockdown conflict and placed on hold.

questions.question: In the Brazil release, how does Compliance dynamic schema store risk and compliance details on change requests?

By adding a new column to the Change Request table for each compliance attribute
In a separate related table with one record per attribute linked to the change request
In the change request work notes as structured journal entries

wrongAnswers.explanation: This reverses the documented behavior: the feature avoids adding columns to the Change Request table.
The release notes say the details are saved in a single field as name and value pairs, not in a separate related table.
The release notes describe storage in a single field via Dynamic Schema, not in work notes.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Change Management

source.excerpt: Compliance dynamic schema saves these details as name and value pairs in a single field using the platform Dynamic Schema feature.

questions.question: In the Brazil release, an incident is placed in the On Hold state with the reason Awaiting Caller Information and the caller never responds to any of the reminder notifications. What happens once all attempts are exhausted?

options.text: The incident is automatically resolved with the resolution code Resolved - No response from caller
The incident is automatically cancelled and the caller is notified
The incident moves back to In Progress and is reassigned to the assignment group manager
The incident stays On Hold until an agent manually resolves it

explanation.correct: With the auto resolve On-Hold incident feature, if the caller does not respond after all attempts are exhausted, the incident is automatically resolved with the resolution code Resolved - No response from caller and a resolution note indicating no caller response. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-incidentmanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say the incident is resolved, not cancelled.
The release notes say the incident moves to In Progress only when the caller responds; with no response it is resolved.
This reverses the documented behavior: the incident is resolved automatically after the attempts are exhausted.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Incident Management

source.excerpt: If the caller does not respond after all attempts are exhausted, the incident is automatically resolved with the resolution code Resolved - No response from caller.
